Both dates are included. Lists use seasonal evidence across available years, not a forecast for the selected year. Maximum range: 366 days.

Where?

Choose from left to right. Each list shows up to 20 locations before scrolling; selecting a place reveals its subregions. Hotspots appear only when there are no further subregions.

Seasonal species and photo coverage

    Photo quizzes are available for this first version. Geography-aware audio selection will need its own coverage checks. Geography quiz answers do not change your saved statistics. Seasonal NC lists use the eBird Basic Dataset, provided by the Cornell Lab of Ornithology.

    Checking “Show all families” lets you see families that are not represented in the current species list. Selecting one of those families will produce no eligible species for this scope.

    Sets Questions to one per eligible species with photos.

    Choose the dates you want to practice for. Both endpoints are included, and the range can span New Year but cannot exceed 366 days. Species lists use observations from the same seasonal window across available years; they are not a forecast for your visit year.

    Select a year and month, then press “Use this month” to fill the start and end dates with that entire calendar month. February includes February 29 in a leap year. You can edit either date afterward.

    Browse from continent to country, then through any subregions to a hotspot or site. A selected country, region, or site scopes the quiz to that place. Location browsing is broader than current quiz coverage: some places do not yet have a supported seasonal species list.

    Expand this list to see species that pass the selected location, dates, rarity setting, and family filter. “Reported in” counts the sampled seasons with records, not the chance of seeing the bird. Species need photo references to enter a photo quiz. A reference does not guarantee that Cornell can deliver the image or that its plumage matches your selected dates.

    A season is your selected date window in an available year. When at least two seasons have been sampled, the default list excludes species reported in only one of them. Checking this includes those records, which may represent rarities or one-time occurrences. Sparse coverage can also cause a species to appear in just one season; this setting is not a reliable rarity classification.

    Limit practice to one bird family, or choose “All families” to practice the whole eligible list. Families remain in taxonomic order and show English and scientific names. By default, only families represented in the current species list are shown; “Show all families” reveals the others.

    Enter how many questions you want, from 1 to 10,000. If a regular quiz has more questions than eligible species, it uses each species once per round and reshuffles for the next round. Turn on “Use all eligible species” to set exactly one question per eligible species.

    Set Questions to exactly the number of eligible species with photos, with one question per species. The count updates when you change location, dates, rarity settings, or family. Questions is read-only while checked; uncheck it to enter a custom count.

    Keep recent practice statistics in this browser?

    With your permission, AviQuiz keeps aggregate statistics covering your five most recent completed quizzes on this device. Small contribution totals keep that rolling window accurate and support retries if the connection fails; this is not a quiz archive. You can take quizzes without allowing browser statistics storage.

    Signed-in account history is a separate setting on the Statistics page. No advertising or tracking cookies are used for these statistics. We remember your storage choice even if you decline.

    What AviQuiz stores in your browser

    If allowed, we keep species-level correct and attempted counts for a rolling window of five quizzes across visual and audio practice, a bounded recent-mistake buffer, and the latest comparison results. Small contribution totals, scope, medium, and synchronization identifiers let us remove old contributions and avoid duplicate uploads. We do not keep a question-by-question quiz archive, your guesses, passwords, or media files.

    We retain one small storage-choice flag so we can honor your decision. Sign-in uses essential session storage. Personal photo review marks are stored separately by the review feature. Browser statistics permission does not control those records or account history.

    Older statistics already present in this browser are preserved until you explicitly import them into your account. They contain rolling answers and latest results, not a complete dated quiz log. New quizzes do not grow that old snapshot. Export it before clearing browser data if you want an additional backup.

    You can change browser statistics permission on the Statistics page. Declining removes the recent-quiz cache; existing unimported history is preserved to avoid accidental loss.
